title: America At War With Iran: Preparation For Conflict

sense.text: These scriptures are the Bible speaking about prophecy: what does the scripture say about prophecy? “I will yet make doctrine to shine as the morning, and will send forth her light afar off.”
“I will yet pour out doctrine as prophecy, and leave it to all ages for ever.” The doctrine is poured out as prophecy, and it is left for all ages, ours included.
“Behold that I have not laboured for myself”: we don’t do this work, this labour, for ourselves, the Bible says. It is “for all them that seek wisdom.”

precepts.why:
“Blessed is he that readeth, and they that hear the words of this prophecy, and keep those things which are written therein.”

What is written in the scriptures? The laws of the Most High God. So blessed are we when we read the prophecy and keep the things that are written in the law.

“We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed.” Take heed to do what the scriptures say. The Most High God called us into this truth, so we have to take heed of that.

“As unto a light that shineth in a dark place”: we are that light shining in a dark place. That is why Christ said, let your light so shine before men. We have to be that example for our people, to win them over into the faith. Whether you are in DC, in New Orleans, in California or in the UK, the Most High chose us, and through our example we have to win our people over.

“Knowing this first”: keep this in mind, “that no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation. For the prophecy”, the foretelling of future events in the Bible, “came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.” Holy men of God: holy black men, holy Hispanic men.

sense.text: “Behold, speak thou in the ears of my people the words of prophecy, which I will put in thy mouth, saith the Lord.” Speak in the ears of my people: that is why we are not sent to a people of a strange speech. We have to deal with our people.
“And cause them to be written in paper”: the prophecy was caused to be written in paper, “for they are faithful and true.” Everything written in the Bible is faithful and true.

“Fear not the imaginations against thee.” Don’t fear what the nations are going to do to us for teaching against America and teaching against the governments. The Bible says don’t fear. “Let not the incredulity of them trouble thee, that speak against thee. For all the unfaithful shall die in their unfaithfulness.”

“Behold, saith the Lord, I will bring plagues upon the world; the sword, famine, death, and destruction.” The Most High is going to bring judgment upon the world.

Keep this in mind: when we are teaching the Bible, bringing out the prophecy, in the street or in the classes, what are these scriptures supposed to do to our people?

precepts.why:
What is the prophecy supposed to do for us? “Be ye strong therefore, and let not your hands be weak: for your work shall be rewarded.” The days we are living in now are not the time for us to be weak. We are to be strong.

This is what the prophet told King Asa: “And when Asa heard these words, and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage, and put away the abominable idols out of all the land of Judah and Benjamin, and out of the cities which he had taken from mount Ephraim.” When Asa heard the words of the prophecy, he took courage.

So this is what prophecy is supposed to do for us: give us the courage to let go of our idols and our secret sins. We are seeing prophecy unravel right before our eyes. Iran and Israel are going to war, and it is only getting worse; now America is involved. It was a rumour and a talk for years, and now it is unfolding. That means more Israelites are repenting, more of our people and more of our brothers are waking up.

sense.text:
Ezra shows us how we ought to prepare our minds and our spirits. We are in captivity, always working, tired and stressed some days, and the Most High has to remind us that we are living in the last days. So brothers, prepare your minds; sisters, prepare your minds.

“For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the Lord.” The heart is the mind: Ezra had prepared his mind to seek the Lord his God, “and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments.”

precepts.why: Preparing the mind: “Lord, thou hast heard the desire of the humble.” We are the humble. We are supposed to humble ourselves to whatever the Bible says we ought to do. “Thou wilt prepare their heart”: he will prepare our minds, and “thou wilt cause thine ear to hear.”

Preparing our minds and our spirits, because war is imminent. The wars are only going to get worse. What we are seeing now is a birthing pain, and all of us are supposed to rejoice, because the scriptures already told us this was going to happen.

“They that fear the Lord will prepare their hearts.” All of us that fear the Lord will prepare our minds, so that whatever evil comes upon the earth, we will remain faithful in serving the Lord, “and humble their souls in his sight.”

“A man of understanding trusteth in the law; and the law is faithful unto him.” We must trust in the laws of God.

Then this is what we have to do: “Prepare what to say, and so thou shalt be heard.” Prepare what to say in prayer when we speak to the Most High, and so we will be heard. Prepare what to say and teach in the streets, and so we will be heard. We must prepare to lead, guide and organize blacks and Hispanics. “And bind up instruction, and then make answer.”

sense.text:
This is to you brothers, you teachers, you up-and-coming soldiers in the MOV program. “Son of man, I have made thee a watchman.” Who is speaking? The Most High said, I have made thee a watchman. That is why you were called into this truth: to warn our people, to warn Israel that they need to repent.

It is not the Bishop that made you a watchman. It is not the deacons, it is not the captains. The Lord called you to be a watchman “unto the house of Israel: therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me.”

What does the Bible say about America and Iran? The world is scared; everybody is fearful because they want to know what is going to happen. Let’s see what the Lord says.

“I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower.” In Ezekiel he says we are watchmen. Standing upon the watch means being awake and paying attention as a watchman. That is how we must be: as watchmen we must be faithful, and pay attention to the signs of the times. “And will watch to see what he will say unto me, and what I shall answer when I am reproved.”

The Lord answered Habakkuk: “Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.” That he may run to teach: teach what the scripture says, because we are supposed to warn our people.

“For the vision is yet for an appointed time”: a lot of these prophecies are set for an appointed time. “But at the end it shall speak, and not lie”: at the end all these prophecies will speak and not lie. “Though it tarry”, though it may take a long time, “wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry.”

What is in the vision? What does it say about America and Iran, and what is God’s plan? “Behold, saith God, I will call together all the kings of the earth to reverence me”: all the countries of the earth, “which are from the rising of the sun, from the south, from the east, and Libanus.” From the south is the Arab nations; in the east, China and India.

“To turn themselves one against another, and repay the things that they have done to them.”

precepts.why:
This is the precept to 2 Esdras 15. The Lord said he is going to call all the kings of the earth, and Joel says: “For, behold, in those days, and in that time, when I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem, I will also gather all nations.” I will gather all nations; I will call together all the kings of the earth.

“And will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat.” The valley of Jehoshaphat is in the Middle East. So what do we see right now? More nations are putting their attention on the Middle East, and right now the focus is America and Iran.

“And will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Israel.” The Lord is going to plead with the nations there in the Middle East for his people.

sense.text:
When the United States began major combat operations in Iran, Donald Trump said American lives may be lost, but we are doing this not for now, we are doing this for the future. Why would he say that? We have to go to the Bible: what does the Bible say about Iran in the future, and about the Iranians as a global power? “Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them.” America knows this. They know the prophecy says Iran is going to be stirred up against them. The Medes “shall not regard silver; and as for gold, they shall not delight in it.” They don’t need money and they don’t want money. They want vengeance.

Look at the timeline of what America has been doing to Iran. In 2020, the year of COVID and Donald Trump’s last year in office, a US drone strike in Baghdad killed the top Iranian general, Qassem Soleimani. That was big, because a lot of the Arabs respected Soleimani; he was uniting the Arabs, the Houthi rebels, Hamas and Hezbollah, and Trump took him out right before he left. Iran retaliated with missile strikes on US bases. In 2021 and 2022 the Biden administration tried to revive the nuclear deal, but the talks failed as Iran accelerated uranium enrichment to 60%. They won’t tell the truth, but of course it is for weapons, because they know who the big threat is: America. In 2023 Iran-backed groups increased attacks on US bases after the October 7th attacks on Israel; in 2024 there were accusations of Iranian plots against Donald Trump; in 2025 the US and Israel struck Iranian nuclear sites. By February 2026, the reports say, the Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed, a man the Muslim world regarded like the Pope.

What does oppression do? Oppression unites. In their arrogance America does not realize they are only making Iran more powerful, because now they view him as a martyr. When Iran’s president Raisi died in a helicopter crash while Israel was at war with Hamas, they said it was a thick fog. That was by no accident. And while they were negotiating, America and Israel dropped a bomb. You can’t trust the white man. All the way from the time when they stole America, he can’t be trusted.

Iran had been sitting back, holding, not really showing their power, and Iran is more powerful than we think. With the Iron Dome, the navy ships along the coast, the military bases in Iraq and Jordan shooting missiles down, and Israel’s fighter jets, Iran is still managing to penetrate Israel, and they say they are only using their older missiles. A missile that adjusts its course in mid-flight from one country to another: this is the technology our forefathers said they saw in a vision. A lot of us can barely adjust our bill; this technology is beyond us, and this is what the Lord put. That is why you see the dragon tails all over the Israeli skies: the Iron Dome can’t stop this type of missile. This is what the Bible has been foretelling, and what we are in the streets teaching and prophesying about. The Lord put the spirit on the scientists to develop it.

Our power is this Bible. We don’t need missile technology and we don’t need guns. Our power is in the word of God: to foretell that these things are going to happen, so that when the people see it actually happen, they respect this Bible even more.

“For after that in the wisdom of God the world by wisdom knew not God, it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe.” What we are doing, teaching in the street, is like foolishness. But the Lord is going to use the teaching of the Bible to bring America down. That is what he is going to use.

So when we see this war, we are supposed to rejoice. It is supposed to increase our faith and have us say, I have to stay in the spirit, we have to fight, because we are drawing closer. As we draw closer to Christ’s return, we have to draw closer to each other: fellowship more, fast and pray more. The Lord is going to return, but this is the time for us to get ourselves right and get our minds strong.

Iran is not just fighting America. Iran is fighting America, Israel, Saudi Arabia, Iraq and Jordan, multiple countries. That shows there are still a lot of prophecies that have to be fulfilled.

“Behold an horrible vision, and the appearance thereof from the east: where the nations of the dragons of Arabia shall come out with many chariots, and the multitude of them shall be carried as the wind upon earth, that all they which hear them may fear and tremble.” This prophecy is not even fulfilled yet. It lets us know the Arab world has to unite, and right now the Arab world is against Iran; it is not united. What we are seeing is a birth pain: as we get closer to Christ’s return it is like a woman in travail. We still have to see the Arab world unite, and according to the scriptures we are going to see terrorism rise. But what is going on now is getting closer.

“Also the Carmanians”, the Iranians, together with the Arab world, “raging in wrath shall go forth as the wild boars of the wood, and with great power shall they come, and join battle with them”, with the Arabs, “and shall waste a portion of the land of the Assyrians.” The land of the Assyrians is Israel.

The casualty numbers we are shown are not accurate. America and Israel scale them down as psychological warfare, to make you believe Iran isn’t that powerful. And look what America did: they bombed a school, 165 schoolgirls. This man is wicked as hell. Now Iran has sent a newer technology, a cluster missile: one ballistic missile that turned into 80 missiles. How is the Iron Dome going to stop that?

This is about the oppressor, Babylon the Great. “Hear thou, I will talk with thee, and the Highest shall say unto thee”, “Art not thou it that remainest of the four beasts, whom I made to reign in my world”: this is America. “That the end of their times might come through them”: through this white man, through America.

“And the fourth came, and overcame all the beasts that were past, and had power over the world with great fearfulness, and over the whole compass of the earth with much wicked oppression; and so long time dwelt he upon the earth with deceit.” That fourth beast was technically Rome, but America is an extension of it.

“For the earth hast thou not judged with truth.” “For thou hast afflicted the meek, thou hast hurt the peaceable, thou hast loved liars”: those are your lawyers. Not all lawyers are wicked; some of our brothers have good intent as lawyers. This is the dirty, grimy lawyers, those that manipulate the law to do America’s bidding. “And destroyed the dwellings of them that brought forth fruit”, and “cast down the walls of such as did thee no harm.”

precepts.why:
“Because thou hast spoiled many nations, all the remnant of the people shall spoil thee.” America has spoiled many nations, and now we see it is America and Israel, Trump and Netanyahu.

What is the reason? “Because of men’s blood, and for the violence of the land, of the city, and of all that dwell therein.”

sense.text: Why are these nations mad? They are mad because of America being a tyrant. “Babylon hath been a golden cup in the Lord’s hand, that made all the earth drunken: the nations have drunken of her wine”: her lies and philosophies. “Therefore the nations are mad.” They are angry, and the scripture gives you the reason why: they have drunken the lies, they have drunken the philosophies.

precepts.why: Here is the precept. Instead of wine, look at the word Daniel uses: “And through his policy.” His policy is the wine. “also he shall cause craft to prosper in his hand; and he shall magnify himself in his heart.”

sense.text: Isaiah saw a vision, and we have to pay attention to the vision Isaiah saw: “The burden of Babylon”.

“Lift ye up a banner upon the high mountain.” The high mountain represents the government, America. What is the banner we ought to lift up? The Bible. In the midst of all this chaos, Isaiah sees the prophets going out teaching.

“Exalt the voice unto them”: that is what we do. We spare not; we lift up our voice as a trumpet. “Shake the hand”: warn our people, “that they may go into the gates of the nobles.” War is coming, and Isaiah sees that in the midst of all this war, the prophets are still going out.

“Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord, we persuade men.” What must we do? Persuade men, because we know what the Lord is going to do. We are the watchmen the Lord set up, and since we know the terror of the Lord, we must persuade men. “But we are made manifest unto God; and I trust also are made manifest in your consciences.”

Who are we trying to persuade? Our people, in the midst of all kinds of sins. Brothers, we must be studying, so that when we come across our people we are able to help them. The whole head is sick; we are sick individuals. But we must learn to discipline ourselves, and we must learn how to persuade our people to change their life.

These are the type of people we are trying to get to change. “Knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane”: it is for our people that are lawless.

“For murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers.” If you knew a brother murdered his father or his mother, you would not treat him the same. Your instant reaction is, bro, you cold, something’s wrong with you. But there is repentance for those spirits. “For manslayers”: you’re cool with a brother and you didn’t know the whole time he got bodies on him. These are the spirits we are trying to win over and get to submit to the Lord.

“For whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind”: women having sex with all kinds of men, men having sex with all kinds of women; defiling themselves with mankind is homosexuality. There is repentance for all these sins. Some of us are struggling with one of these, two, three, four, five of these. God damn. We have demons on us, and the only way to get them out is to open up to the counsel of a thousand. Some of you don’t want to open up, so by the time we find out what you are struggling with, it is too late to help you. You can still repent, but it is a lot harder because you kept it secret so long, and by the time you tell us you are already having sex and we have to throw you out. Repent. Submit yourself to the Lord. Stay close with the pack.

“For menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine.” We all lie. Bro, why didn’t you come to the Sabbath? Oh man, my back, I was tired. Lie. Why didn’t you come to the new moon? I got off of work. Lie. In your mind you said, I’ll go next time, and you felt convicted when a brother or a sister asked you.

Our people are sinning in all these sins in front of our eyes, and we have to persuade them. Can you persuade a murderer to change his life? A lesbian, a homosexual? Can you turn a liar, a thief, into a soldier? You can, and the proof is you sitting right here in the building. You may say, only Deacon Ithan knows how to do that, only Black Rhino knows how to talk to people, I’m a quiet, shy person. But you don’t know what the Lord sees.

precepts.why:
This is what we have to overcome. “Surely he knoweth your inventions, and what ye think in your hearts, even them that sin, and would hide their sin.” That is what we do: we sin and we hide our sin. The Lord says, I know your inventions. I know why you watch HBO at night, why you like Spartacus, why you like Power. I know you love to smoke weed and spray yourself with cologne right before you go to the Sabbath, and then security says that brother smells like weed. Keep smoking weed, brothers and sisters, and you are going to end up in handcuffs on the ground.

Some of you brothers are married at home to an unbelieving woman. We want to raise you up to a soldier, but we can’t, because you refuse to apply the scriptures. She doesn’t believe, she’s cooking pork on the other half of the grill next to your lawful food, she’s still going to the club, she doesn’t respect you, and you refuse to leave these crazy women. Some of these women are toxic, and it isn’t just Dominicans; it’s Judah too. Judah women ain’t right, Benjamin women ain’t right, especially Benjamin women: they always ice grill you when you go to the restaurant. There’s no love amongst our people.

We get caught up in these sins: brothers tied to unbelieving women, women tied to unbelieving men, smoking weed, doing all kinds of evil. We fall in the category of 1 Timothy 1:9. We’re lawless.

sense.text: “That there should not be such heaviness in their destruction, as shall be joy over them that are persuaded to salvation.” We must persuade men to salvation. We see the wars going on with Iran, we see the prophecies coming to pass and escalating, but the Lord told us: go persuade my people to salvation, go bring them into the sanctuary. How do we do that?

This is one of the keys. We must get ourselves right and get ourselves together, but here is what we must also do: “By long forbearing is a prince persuaded.” To forbear is to restrain patiently, to have patience. A prince is a very high rank, and the scripture says that with long patience you can persuade even princes. What does Israel mean? Prince of the power. So we have to be patient with the Israelites, with our people, and then we will be able to persuade them.

As teachers we have to be patient with our people. Be strategic. When you’re having that conversation, don’t think, they’re just wicked as hell. They might actually repent, but you’re not patient enough. You have to be diplomatic and know how to reason with people. When people come up to you in the street, don’t give them the first death scripture. You were once in that spot; the only reason we are in this building is that the Lord opened our eyes.

“And a soft tongue breaketh the bone”: a wise response. Somebody can be pissed with you, and you respond with peace, and that breaks the bone. But y’all from Brooklyn, y’all from DC, you want to respond even more aggressive. I’m from PG County. Listen. Remember, we have to be patient with our people.
Isaiah gives us an analogy of a farmer. But is Isaiah really talking about farmland? “Give ye ear, and hear my voice; hearken, and hear my speech.” The Lord is telling us to listen to him.

“Doth the plowman plow all day to sow? doth he open and break the clods of his ground?” The plowman dealing with his farm has to break the dirt. But the plowing represents teaching: we are to plow in hope, to give hope to our people. Teach. Instruct.

“When he hath made plain the face thereof”: he makes the whole ground flat, because he is preparing to throw his seed so it can grow. “Doth he not cast abroad the fitches, and scatter the cummin, and cast in the principal wheat and the appointed barley”, and the rye: each is a seed he casts abroad the field.

The fitches are a very delicate seed; you have to be very careful how you deal with them. The rye can grow in almost any environment, even in the wintertime. The appointed barley is in the middle. Five seeds: the Lord is telling us that when we deal with our people we are going to be dealing with different personalities. Some are going to be very petite and soft, some hard like rye, some in the middle.

It wasn’t really talking about farming. It is talking about learning how to deal with different people: brothers who were murderers, brothers with a sex problem, brothers with an anger issue, brothers who don’t know how to raise their children, sisters with psychological hang-ups, sisters who came out of jail. There are all kinds of spirits out there, and you have to know how to persuade them to salvation, adjusting your spirit to bring them into the fold.

The barley is appointed, timely: there is a time to grow barley and a time to bring out certain things. You have to know when to use the tools you have, when to show mercy and when to be strong and assertive, and who you are talking to. You have to be diplomatic.

“For his God doth instruct him to discretion, and doth teach him.” The farmer knew that to grow the fitches it has to be in this season, and he has to be very delicate with that seed. The Lord will teach us how to be discreet: careful and circumspect in one’s speech or actions, especially in order to avoid causing offence or to gain an advantage.

Ask yourself: are you careful in your speech and your actions when you are dealing with people and trying to win them over? Learn discernment. Learn how to speak to people in order to win them over. You know how to speak, and you know when to speak: that is discretion, and we have to do it to bring souls into this truth.

“For the fitches are not threshed with a threshing instrument”: you cannot use a threshing instrument on that kind of seed. “Neither is a cart wheel turned about upon the cummin”: you would destroy it. “But the fitches are beaten out with a staff, and the cummin with a rod.” The Lord is saying you have to use specific instruments for each kind of seed.

“Bread corn is bruised; because he will not ever be threshing it, nor break it with the wheel of his cart, nor bruise it with his horsemen.” We have to be strategic about how we grow the farm, using the right instrument for each seed.

precepts.why:
“For our sakes, no doubt, this is written: that he that ploweth should plow in hope.” It wasn’t really talking about farms. As a plowman, you are to plow in hope. “And that he that thresheth in hope should be partaker of his hope.”

So the plowing and the threshing in Isaiah 28 were not really about growing seeds. You are fishers of men, and this is how it applies to you: the plowing is the teaching, and we are to give hope to our people.

sense.text:
You may be saying, I’m teaching this brother, I’m putting my time in, but he won’t come to the school, I don’t get it. Are you really discerning how to deal with that brother? At the end of the day the Lord brings them in, but are you doing your job to bring them in? We are at war. Russia is about to get involved, China is going to get involved; it is only going to get worse. We have to be better fishermen.

“To every thing there is a season.” Not to some things: to every thing. So when we are fishing, there is a time to talk about the truth with that brother. Sometimes you are talking about the truth out of season; it wasn’t the right time to bring it up, and you didn’t discern it. You say, this brother won’t listen, but he was stressed from work, things were going on, his mind just wasn’t open. If you pay attention and watch, you will see it. Then one day the brother says, I was watching this documentary and I’m starting to think this world isn’t really what I thought it was. That’s it: you waited two years for that moment, and he opened up. Be patient with your brothers and sisters.

precepts.why:
Even the disciples were in the spirit, but Christ rebuked them for it. “And sent messengers before his face: and they went, and entered into a village of the Samaritans, to make ready for him. And they did not receive him”, Christ, “because his face was as though he would go to Jerusalem.”

“And when his disciples James and John saw this, they said, Lord, wilt thou that we command fire to come down from heaven, and consume them”: let’s go get the death scriptures and pray to the Lord to take them out. “But he turned, and rebuked them, and said, Ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of.”

Brothers, you have to know what manner of spirit you are supposed to be in when you are dealing with the people in the street. Sisters, the same way: sometimes the brothers do the work and the people come in, and then the sisters undo the work because they won’t say hello, shalom, or Christ bless. Brothers, you are fishers of men, and sisters need to learn how to fish too. Always represent this truth with the utmost professionalism, because we have a job: to win souls, and it is only going to get worse and we don’t have much time.

Always be on duty to win somebody over. As soon as you step into a room or a store, you should already be mapping out who you could bring the truth to. You don’t need to be a soldier to do that. Brother O’Shea in New York is 83, and he hands out his 50 flyers a week; the lady from the nursing home he spoke to started wearing dresses. He is fishing even with his home health aide. We must be fishers of men, because war is imminent and danger is coming.

sense.text:
We spoke about America, about Iran, about repentance and how to fish. Now, what is the end result for us? What are our blessings?

“The burden of the word of the Lord in the land of Hadrach, and Damascus shall be the rest thereof.” Damascus is in Syria, and Syria is going to be involved in this last world war. Why do you think they took out Bashar al-Assad? They had been trying to get him out for years, and they finally got him out. “When the eyes of man, as of all the tribes of Israel, shall be toward the Lord”: we all need to get our eyes toward the Lord.

“And Hamath also shall border thereby; Tyrus, and Zidon, though it be very wise.” He is giving you locations: Tyre and Zidon is where Lebanon is. “And Tyrus did build herself a strong hold, and heaped up silver as the dust, and fine gold as the mire of the streets.”
This is future prophecy. “Behold, the Lord will cast her out, and he will smite her power in the sea; and she shall be devoured with fire.” Tyre shall be devoured with fire.

“Ashkelon shall see it, and fear.” Ashkelon is in Israel. They are going to see the judgment: the bombs, the terror, and they are going to fear. “Gaza also shall see it, and be very sorrowful”: these countries are going to see the judgment that comes upon Israel. “and Ashkelon shall not be inhabited”, because it is going to be total destruction.
“And a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod.” Is there a bastard in Ashdod now? Yes. Zechariah was right with what he saw. “And I will cut off the pride of the Philistines”: the pride of the Palestinians.

“And I will take away his blood out of his mouth, and his abominations from between his teeth: but he that remaineth, even he, shall be for our God.” Brothers, do you want to remain? You want to be for our God, but we must remain. “And he shall be as a governor in Judah, and Ekron as a Jebusite.”

“And I will encamp about mine house because of the army, because of him that passeth by, and because of him that returneth: and no oppressor shall pass through them any more.” We are tired of the oppression, tired of oppressors. Judgment is going to come in the Middle East; Zechariah saw it, and we are seeing it unfold slowly. “For now have I seen with mine eyes.”

“Rejoice greatly”: not a small rejoicing, greatly. “O daughter of Zion”: that is who we are. “Shout, O daughter of Jerusalem”: shout, you blacks, and shout, you Hispanics. “Behold, thy King cometh unto thee”: Christ is coming. “He is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass.” That was fulfilled in that time, but he is going to come back. Christ is going to return.

“And I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim, and the horse from Jerusalem, and the battle bow shall be cut off”: this is all judgment. “And he shall speak peace unto the heathen: and his dominion shall be from sea even to sea, and from the river even to the ends of the earth”, because our people are scattered. He is going to conquer and be over all.

“As for thee also, by the blood of thy covenant I have sent forth thy prisoners.” We are those prisoners: we are in captivity, under oppression. “Out of the pit wherein is no water”: out of the pit wherein is no truth.

“Turn you to the strong hold.” Even in the midst of our sins we must repent and turn to the stronghold, and the stronghold is the Bible. “Ye prisoners of hope”: we are prisoners of hope, crying late at night and praying, Lord, I need you to help me overcome my sin. “Even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee.” The Lord says he will render double unto us. Don’t worry; just be faithful.

“When I have bent Judah for me”: Judah is going to be humbled; Judah is going to repent. “Filled the bow with Ephraim”: all the Puerto Ricans and Hispanics are going to join and help Judah. “And raised up thy sons, O Zion”: the Lord is raising up our sons now, “against thy sons, O Greece, and made thee as the sword of a mighty man.” He is showing you a man, a warrior: Judah the bow, Ephraim filling it, a soldier going to war against the sons of Greece.

“And the Lord shall be seen over them”: in the wilderness, when we make it out, the Lord shall be seen over us. “And his arrow shall go forth as the lightning: and the Lord God shall blow the trumpet, and shall go with whirlwinds of the south.”
